en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-aryabuddhamātṛ-prajñāpāramitā-sūkṣmākṣara-sūtra*,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of Milin Monastery in Jalandhara, Central India, during the Western Heavens (India).
The Śramaṇa of Purple Robes, the Subject Tianxi’ai, respectfully translated by imperial decree: Thus have I heard:

At one time, the World-Honored One was dwelling on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus, as well as hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas. Furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Brahmā kings, Śakra devānām indra, and the world-protectors, along with a vast multitude of other beings, all surrounding him with reverent devotion.
At that time, the World-Honored One sat cross-legged upon the auspicious jewel-treasury lion throne.

Then, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, and knelt with his right knee on the ground. Gazing up at the Honored One’s head without averting his eyes for a moment, he joined his palms in reverence, leaped for joy, and prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, addressing him thus:
“World-Honored One!
I only pray that the World-Honored One will expound for me this *Svalpākṣara-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*,
so that all sentient beings may hear this Dharma, obtain great merit and virtue, have all their karmic obstructions definitively eliminated, and swiftly attain unsurpassed bodhi in the future.

If there are sentient beings who give rise to a heart of utmost sincerity and receive, uphold, read, and recite this mantra, whatever aspirations they seek shall be definitively accomplished, free from all demonic obstacles.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara:
“Excellent! Excellent is this speech. Excellent, excellent!”
"Good son!
You are able to thus serve all sentient beings with a sincere heart, enabling them to attain peace, happiness, long life, and well-being.
Good son!"
You should listen attentively and with a sincere mind as I expound this *Svalpākṣarā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.

If any sentient beings hear this Dharma being taught, they will obtain great merit and virtue; all their karmic obstructions will be completely eliminated, and they will certainly and swiftly realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"If there are sentient beings who resolve their minds to receive and uphold this mantra, they will be free from all demonic obstacles and shall all attain accomplishment.
At that time, the Holy Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"The Sugata now speaks this for the sake of all sentient beings, so that they may attain peace and happiness.
At that time, the World-Honored One entered a samādhi called "Liberating All Sentient Beings."
Having arisen from meditative concentration, a tuft of white hair between his eyebrows emitted hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of light rays.

This great radiance universally illumined all Buddha-fields; all immeasurable sentient beings who were touched by its light attained the certainty of swiftly realizing anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and all sentient beings in the hells obtained peace and happiness.
The buddha-fields shook in six ways, and upon each Buddha there fell a rain of exquisite sandalwood, aloeswood, and fine powdered incense as an offering.
At that time, as the World-Honored One was preaching this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra,

all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each gave rise to a mind of equanimity, a mind of loving-kindness and compassion, a mind of mindfulness directed toward the benefit of others, a mind of being free from all karmic obstructions, a mind of various kinds of benefit, and a mind of prajñāpāramitā.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara:
“Listen attentively; I shall now recite for you this mantra of the Shorter Prajñāpāramitā, the Holy Mother of the Buddhas, which is as follows:”
"Namo śrī-munaye tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | tadyathā | muni mune mahāmune svāhā. The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ārya Avalokiteśvara, saying:

"This mantra of the Minor Prajñāpāramitā of the Noble Mother of Buddhas is that by which all Buddhas have attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; I, too, have attained unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by means of this mantra of the Minor Prajñāpāramitā."
In the past, there was a Buddha also named Śākyamuni Tathāgata; at that Buddha’s place, he heard this Dharma being taught. That Buddha said:
"Thus, all Buddhas of the three periods of time have attained Buddhahood only by means of this Dharma."
The Buddha again addressed the Holy Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"I now bestow upon you this prediction:
in a future age within the human realm, you shall attain the Way of the Buddha, and your name shall be the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Universal Radiance Auspicious Jewel-Peak King."

Having heard such a sublime Dharma as this, you should receive, uphold, read, and recite it; whether you write it yourself or instruct others to write it, contemplate and comprehend it, and furthermore, extensively explain its meaning to all other sentient beings, causing them to copy this sutra and receive, uphold, read, and recite it within their own homes, so that they may swiftly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in future ages.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas will bear witness to you.
Now, for your sake, I shall further recite the Prajñāpāramitā Dhāraṇī, which says:
"Tadyathā... (Tadyathā).
Oṃ jaya jaya padmābhe.
Avameṃ (4) sarvānī (5) vili vili (6)
Vīra vīri cili cili nivarta nūṃ.
Phalaṃ kṣiṇi 10. Muditāraṇi 11. Praraṇi 12.
bhūrja 13 pāgavante 14 sarvārthe 15.
Mama, here is called the name:
(16) *ṣoḍaśapūraya* (17) *sarvasattvānām* (18).
Sarvajñama-vāraṇakṣi viśodhaya. (19–21)
VĪŚU DĀYA (22) BUDDHADEŚITĀNĪM (23) SVĀHĀ (24).
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Holy Avalokiteśvara:
"This sublime Dharma, the Prajñāpāramitā Dhāraṇī, is the mother who gives birth to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
If any sentient beings hear this Dharma even for a moment, all the karmic obstructions they have created will be completely extinguished."
Regarding this dharma, all Buddhas and bodhisattvas could not exhaustively describe its merits even after speaking for a hundred koṭis of kalpas.
If one can receive, uphold, read, and recite this dhāraṇī, one will enter into all maṇḍalas and receive empowerment.
"Furthermore, it is like upholding all mantras, wherein one attains accomplishment in each case.
At that time, the Holy Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"For what reason, furthermore, is this *prajñāpāramitā-dhāraṇī* taught?
The World-Honored One replied,
"Out of compassion for all sentient beings who possess little skillful means and are indolent, I have therefore taught this *prajñāpāramitā-dhāraṇī*."
They shall cause those beings to receive, uphold, read, and recite it, whether by writing it themselves or instructing others to write it.
All such sentient beings will swiftly realize unsurpassed bodhi.
"So it is, so it is! The Blessed One has well spoken this Prajñāpāramitā dhāraṇī.
At that time, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This Dharma is truly unprecedented.
World-Honored One!”
This Dharma is truly unprecedented.

Out of great compassion, the World-Honored One, the Well-Gone One, has preached this wondrous Dharma in order to deliver all sentient beings who possess little merit, few skillful means, and are indolent, so that they may obtain benefit, peace, and happiness.

At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished preaching this sutra, all the great śrāvakas and the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as well as all those in the world—gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas—hearing what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they accepted it with faith, practiced accordingly, prostrated themselves, and withdrew.
The Sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom in Few Syllables, the Noble Mother of the Buddhas, Spoken by the Buddha.
